title: Hosted vs. Self-Hosted Model Decision
summary: Choose a managed API, cloud deployment, managed compute, or self-hosted model from workload, data, reliability, staffing, and total-cost evidence.
prerequisites: Expected traffic, latency, availability, and recovery targets
An owner for model and infrastructure operations

sections.title: Separate access model from infrastructure model
paragraphs: Start by separating four deployment paths. A direct managed provider API outsources model serving, routine availability operations, and much of scaling, while retaining dependencies on provider availability, quota, lifecycle, and data boundaries. The customer still owns application integration, data authorization, provider configuration, quality and safety acceptance, fallback, and incident coordination. A cloud catalog or serverless API adds customer controls for tenant, identity, network, region, capacity choice, and application behavior without requiring the customer to operate model-serving infrastructure. Managed compute is a dedicated compute service in which the provider operates the platform and, where documented, the serving runtime, base images, and patching. The customer owns model artifact and license verification, deployment configuration, capacity, application controls, quality and safety acceptance, fallback, and remaining operations. Customer-operated self-hosting makes the customer responsible for weights and license, serving runtime, images, hardware, networking, scaling, patching, observability, safety controls, incidents, backups, restore, and recovery.

These categories describe operational responsibility boundaries, not model categories. The same model family may be offered through different deployment paths. A deployment path does not establish that a particular model variant is available, appropriately licensed, performant, or suitable for production.

Microsoft Foundry documentation describes serverless API deployment types including standard, provisioned, and batch. The documentation checked on 2026-09-19 describes Managed compute as preview dedicated GPU PaaS with Microsoft-owned serving runtime, base images, and patching. It also reports no SLA, global processing, and no built-in content filtering for that preview path, and says it is not recommended for production. These properties must not be generalized to every model or SKU. Check the exact catalog entry and SKU before relying on them. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/deployments-overview

A model listing is not deployment approval. Hugging Face model documentation describes model cards, evaluations, gated models, downloads, licenses, inference information, and hardware information. A listing does not by itself prove license suitability, quality, available hardware capacity, or production fitness. For any candidate, record the exact model identifier, artifact digest, source, license text and obligations, runtime version, quantization format, hardware test, and deployment path. Source: https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/models

Candidate coverage should be broad enough to avoid treating one vendor or family as the default. Candidates may include Meta Llama, DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral, Microsoft Phi, NVIDIA Nemotron, Z.ai, and other families. This list makes no claim about the availability, license, capability, or production suitability of any exact variant. Check the exact artifact and terms. Azure documentation for models sold directly by Azure is available at https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/models-sold-directly-by-azure

Locality is not the same as privacy. A local deployment can still expose data through logs, backups, support access, telemetry, or a compromised host. A hosted deployment may satisfy a data boundary only if its tenant, region, retention, identity, network, and provider terms are verified. Do not infer security, privacy, quality, lower cost, or reliability from the word local.

code.label: Option responsibility matrix
code.code:
Option: direct managed provider API
Provider owns: serving infrastructure, routine availability operations, much of scaling
Customer still owns: application integration, data authorization, provider configuration, quality and safety acceptance, fallback, incident coordination
Typical dependency: provider quota, lifecycle, retention, region, and service availability

Option: cloud catalog or serverless API
Provider owns: catalog service and serving infrastructure for the selected deployment type
Customer owns: tenant, identity, network, region, capacity choice, application controls, quality and safety acceptance, fallback
Typical dependency: model and SKU availability, quota, region, and catalog terms

Option: managed compute
Provider owns: managed compute platform and, where documented, serving runtime, base images, and patching
Customer owns: model artifact and license verification, deployment configuration, capacity, application controls, quality and safety acceptance, fallback, and remaining operations
Typical dependency: preview or service limitations, hardware and SKU availability, processing behavior, and support terms

Option: customer-operated self-hosting
Customer owns: weights and license, serving runtime, images, hardware, networking, scaling, patching, observability, safety controls, incidents, backups, restore, and recovery
Typical dependency: customer staffing, hardware supply, power, and operational maturity

sections.callout: First compare hard constraints. A lower calculated subtotal cannot repair a license gap, disconnected-operation failure, unacceptable data path, missing SLO evidence, or unowned operational work.

sections.title: Model the real workload and failure boundary
paragraphs: Use the same demand and acceptance tests for every viable path. Record normal and burst concurrency, requests per minute, input and output tokens, tool calls, latency distribution including cold start and tail latency, availability, recovery time, data retention, egress, safety controls, regional processing, support, and the cost of keeping a safe fallback.

For these teaching cases, one staff-month is defined as 160 available staff-hours. Therefore, 0.15 staff-month equals 24 available staff-hours per month. This is an explicit planning convention, not a universal payroll or industry definition. A staffing gate is not decided from hours alone. Each selected shape must have a named primary owner, a named backup, an on-call or escalation arrangement, and enough time for monitoring, patching, incident response, testing, and recovery. If those assignments and coverage are not documented, the staffing gate fails even if the arithmetic appears to fit.

The following two cases are fictional worked examples. Their rates, capacities, staff hours, Boolean gates, and test outcomes are teaching fixtures. They are not vendor quotes, live deployment evidence, actual benchmarks, contractual commitments, or proof that a real gate passed.

Worked case A, bursty low-volume workload with limited operations staff: A support application has 200 requests per day, 1,200 input tokens and 300 output tokens per request, 2 normal concurrent requests, an 8-request burst, a 2-second interactive target, a monthly availability target of 99.5 percent, and no disconnected requirement. Monthly demand is 200 x 30 x 1,200 = 7,200,000 input tokens and 200 x 30 x 300 = 1,800,000 output tokens. Total demand is 9,000,000 tokens. The team has 0.15 operations staff-month available, defined here as 24 hours. The 12 labor-hours in the managed-compute subtotal are only a cost assumption, not proof of full operational coverage. With no documented backup and on-call arrangement for the remaining provider and customer operations, managed compute fails the staffing gate. Self-hosting's 24 labor-hours consume the entire available allocation and leave no demonstrated owner, backup, or on-call reserve, so it also fails the staffing gate.

For case A, the fictional managed-API price is $0.0008 per 1,000 input tokens plus $0.0020 per 1,000 output tokens, with $180 per month for support and integration controls and $20 per month for estimated egress. The calculation is (7,200 x $0.0008) + (1,800 x $0.0020) + $180 + $20 = $5.76 + $3.60 + $180 + $20 = $209.36 per month. The exact license fee and any unlisted costs are UNKNOWN and are not relabeled as zero. Therefore, $209.36 is a conditional subtotal, not complete TCO. The provisional recommendation is managed API, conditional on passing data-boundary, license, quality, safety, quota, staffing, fallback, and 99.5 percent SLO gates. A conditional recommendation is not approval.

Case A comparison: The fictional cloud catalog or serverless option costs a $250 monthly service allowance plus $60 support, $20 egress, and $120 reserved capacity, producing a $450 conditional subtotal. It meets the stated tenant and region controls in this fictional case, but is rejected on cost because those extra controls are not required after the fictional API data-boundary review. The fictional managed-compute option uses two $900 GPU-month units. Although average utilization is assumed to be 20 percent, the reservation is paid in full: 2 x $900 = $1,800. Adding $40 incremental energy, $30 storage, 12 staff-hours x $80 = $960, $100 monitoring, and $60 recovery gives a $2,990 conditional subtotal. Self-hosting uses $1,500 monthly hardware amortization, $120 energy, $40 storage, 24 staff-hours x $80 = $1,920, $180 monitoring, and $100 recovery, producing a $3,860 conditional subtotal. License cost remains UNKNOWN for all paths until exact terms are checked.

Worked case B, sustained disconnected and local requirement with qualified staff: A plant has 80 requests per minute during a 10-hour operating day, 1,500 input tokens and 300 output tokens per request, required disconnected operation, local data processing, 99.9 percent availability during operating hours, and a 30-minute recovery target. Monthly request volume is 80 x 60 x 10 x 30 = 1,440,000 requests. Planning demand is 80 x 1,800 = 144,000 tokens per minute, or 2,400 tokens per second. The fictional sizing assumption is four locally owned GPU units, each planned at 700 input-and-output-equivalent tokens per second for the selected workload. This gives 4 x 700 = 2,800 tokens per second of installed planning capacity before reserve. The 700-token-per-second value is not a qualified serving measurement. Qualified capacity remains UNKNOWN until representative load, thermal, failure, and recovery testing is completed.

Losing one unit leaves 3 x 700 = 2,100 tokens per second, which is below the 2,400-token-per-second demand. The Case B N-1 gate therefore fails. Four installed units are enough only before the reserved failure is applied. A 99.9 percent SLO also remains UNKNOWN until load distribution, redundancy, failure behavior, and recovery evidence are measured and approved. No Case B deployment is approved by this sizing exercise. The gate requires qualified capacity at demand after the approved failure reserve, or a documented degraded mode accepted by the accountable owner.

For case B, the managed API and cloud catalog or serverless API fail immediately because operation while disconnected from the external service is required. The fictional Foundry managed-compute path also fails this case's hard gate because the documented preview path reports global processing and no SLA, while this workload requires local disconnected operation and 99.9 percent availability. Managed compute is not treated as equivalent to customer-operated self-hosting. Customer-operated self-hosting is only a provisional recommendation after the exact model license, artifact provenance, runtime, quantization, hardware capacity, safety controls, staffing coverage, and restore procedure pass review. It is not approval.

Case B's fictional self-hosting conditional subtotal is $4,800 hardware amortization + $600 energy + $150 storage and local backup + 30 staff-hours x $110 = $3,300 labor + $300 monitoring + $250 recovery = $9,400 per month. The arithmetic does not separately add an idle-capacity charge because the $4,800 hardware amortization already pays for the four installed units. Network egress is $0 under the fictional disconnected-local assumption. License cost is UNKNOWN, not zero. Complete TCO is consequently UNKNOWN until license cost and any other omitted obligations are established.

Sensitivity must change assumptions explicitly. For Case A self-hosting, assume the unchanged demand uses a smaller qualified reservation at 70 percent utilization. Keep hardware amortization, labor, monitoring, and recovery unchanged, but change the fictional energy assumption from $120 to $260. The conditional subtotal becomes $1,500 + $260 + $40 + $1,920 + $180 + $100 = $4,000. Managed API remains at a $209.36 conditional subtotal for the unchanged workload. This sensitivity does not cure self-hosting's missing owner, backup, or on-call coverage.

In Case B, reducing the fictional operator-time assumption from 30 to 10 hours changes the self-hosting conditional subtotal to $4,800 + $600 + $150 + $1,100 + $300 + $250 = $7,200. It does not prove that ten hours is sufficient, provide missing N-1 capacity, or remove the need for local operational ownership. Sensitivity changes cost and staffing risk. It does not waive a hard constraint.

Do not select an option when required evidence is missing. A license gap, prohibited data path, failed security review, unsupported latency or availability target, failed quality or safety gate, unavailable model or SKU, insufficient qualified capacity or failure reserve, or unowned scaling and incident work is a no-go. Record the reason, stop new traffic if a selected shape has failed, route to the verified fallback, reconcile state and side effects, and reopen the decision after evidence is obtained.

code.label: Two filled decisions followed by the original blank template
code.code:
FILLED RECORD A: BURSTY LOW-VOLUME SUPPORT WORKLOAD
Task: Select a deployment path for 200 support requests per day with limited operations staff.
Scope: Non-disconnected support data; one region; exact model artifact to be selected; direct managed API, cloud catalog/serverless API, managed compute, and customer-operated self-hosting considered.
Permissions: Application owner may approve data access and deployment; tenant and network review required for cloud options; exact model license and artifact digest required before approval.
Staffing convention: 1 staff-month = 160 available hours for this teaching case; 0.15 staff-month = 24 hours. A named owner, backup, and on-call/escalation arrangement are mandatory. Hours alone do not establish coverage.
Demand: 200 requests/day; 1,200 input and 300 output tokens/request; 2 normal and 8 burst concurrency; 2-second interactive target; 99.5% monthly availability target.
Option costs: Managed API = (7,200 x $0.0008) + (1,800 x $0.0020) + $180 support/integration + $20 egress = $209.36/month conditional subtotal. Cloud catalog/serverless = $250 allowance + $60 support + $20 egress + $120 reserved capacity = $450/month conditional subtotal. Managed compute = 2 x $900 GPU-month + $40 incremental energy + $30 storage + 12 x $80 labor + $100 monitoring + $60 recovery = $2,990/month conditional subtotal. Self-hosting = $1,500 hardware amortization + $120 energy + $40 storage + 24 x $80 labor + $180 monitoring + $100 recovery = $3,860/month conditional subtotal. License cost: UNKNOWN pending exact terms. Complete TCO: UNKNOWN.
Control boundary: Managed API must pass data retention, identity, region, network, and provider-access review. Customer does not control weights or runtime. Other paths require their stated tenant, artifact, runtime, hardware, and log controls.
Operations: Limited staff cannot approve self-hosting or managed compute without named owner, backup, and on-call evidence. Managed API provider operates serving; customer owns application behavior, authorization, quality, safety, quota, fallback, and incident coordination.
Stop conditions: Any license gap, prohibited provider data path, failed quality or safety gate, unavailable quota, unsupported 2-second or 99.5% target, insufficient staffing coverage, or unowned incident work.
Verification: Synthetic fixture evaluation, representative load test at 2 normal and 8 burst concurrency, p50 and p95 latency, quota test, safety test, retention test, controlled provider-failure test, and subtotal review. Synthetic results and Boolean gates are fictional teaching fixtures, not actual proof.
Recovery: Verified fallback to a recorded simpler response path; reconcile ticket state and tool side effects; test restore and replay before production approval.
Decision: Provisional recommendation: managed API, conditional on all hard gates passing. This is not approval. Cloud catalog/serverless is rejected as unnecessary and more costly in this fictional scope. Managed compute and self-hosting fail the demonstrated staffing-coverage gate and cost comparison.

FILLED RECORD B: SUSTAINED DISCONNECTED PLANT WORKLOAD
Task: Select a deployment path for a plant that must continue operating while disconnected.
Scope: Local plant data only; disconnected mode required; four local GPU units; exact model artifact, runtime, and quantization to be selected; all four paths considered.
Permissions: Plant owner controls local data and hardware; qualified operators are assigned; exact license permits intended use only if verified from the license text.
Demand: 80 requests/minute for 10 operating hours/day; 1,500 input and 300 output tokens/request; 2,400 tokens/second planning demand; 99.9% operating-hours availability; 30-minute recovery target.
Option costs: Managed API = NOT VIABLE because disconnected operation is required. Cloud catalog/serverless = NOT VIABLE because it depends on external connectivity. Managed compute = NOT VIABLE for this case because the documented Foundry preview properties conflict with the local disconnected and 99.9% requirements. Self-hosting = $4,800 hardware amortization + $600 energy + $150 storage/backup + 30 x $110 labor + $300 monitoring + $250 recovery = $9,400/month conditional subtotal. License cost: UNKNOWN. Complete TCO: UNKNOWN.
Capacity: Four planning units x 700 tokens/second = 2,800 installed planning tokens/second. After one unit fails, 3 x 700 = 2,100, below 2,400 demand. The N-1 capacity gate fails. Qualified serving capacity, approved reserve, load distribution, and 99.9% SLO evidence are UNKNOWN until measured.
Control boundary: Customer controls local identity, network, data, weights, runtime, logs, hardware, and backups, subject to security review.
Operations: Qualified staff own scaling, patching, monitoring, incidents, safety controls, restore, and recovery. The four-GPU figure and all Boolean gates are fictional planning fixtures, not measured evidence.
Stop conditions: License or provenance gap, failed local security review, qualified capacity below demand after reserve, failed quality or safety gate, recovery above 30 minutes, failed one-unit reserve test, or unowned patching and incident work.
Verification: Synthetic load plan at 2,400 tokens/second demand after approved reserve; measure p50, p95, and p99 latency, saturation, thermal behavior, power, failover, restore, safety, and offline operation. No actual benchmark result is claimed.
Recovery: Test local replica or spare-node failover, restore from an offline backup, reconcile queued tool effects, and document manual safe operation.
Decision: Provisional recommendation: customer-operated self-hosting because hosted paths fail the disconnected hard constraint, not merely the cost comparison. This is not approval. Approval remains blocked until license, artifact, security, quality, safety, qualified-capacity, failure-reserve, staffing, and recovery gates pass.

sections.callout: All prices, capacities, and Boolean gates in the worked cases are fictional teaching fixtures. Unknown license costs, unverified capacities, and unverified SLO evidence remain UNKNOWN. A conditional recommendation is not approval.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence includes the data boundary, demand model, exact model and runtime artifacts, artifact digest, license and obligations, deployment options, representative quality and safety results, performance distribution, conditional-subtotal assumptions, complete-TCO unknowns, operational owner and backup, on-call or escalation coverage, failure tests, and an expiry date for the decision. Evidence must identify which observations are measured, which come from supplier documentation, which are contractual, which are fictional fixtures, and which remain UNKNOWN.

Use an exact measured-evidence plan. First, freeze a representative fixture set with input classes, expected behavior, safety cases, tool-call cases, and disallowed data. Second, record the exact model identifier, weight digest, tokenizer, runtime, quantization, accelerator type, image digest, configuration, and deployment SKU. Third, run warm-up and cold-start tests at normal and burst concurrency. Measure requests per second, input and output tokens per second, p50, p95, and p99 latency, errors, queue time, saturation, memory, power, and recovery time. Fourth, run quality, safety, prompt-injection, data-boundary, retention, identity, and network tests. Fifth, test provider failure, GPU failure, restore, replay, duplicate side effects, and fallback reconciliation. Sixth, retain raw results, test code, timestamps, region, configuration, staffing assignments, and expiry date.

Synthetic worked evidence is for teaching only. For Case A, the fixture contains 12 support prompts, 3 safety prompts, 2 quota-error scenarios, and 1 provider-failure scenario. A fictional Boolean result can show how a gate controls the exercise, but it is not proof that a real license, data boundary, SLO, staffing arrangement, or deployment passed. For Case B, the fictional checklist records an offline network test, a four-GPU planning shape, a restore drill, and a side-effect reconciliation drill. Qualified capacity, failure reserve, SLO, and recovery outcomes remain UNKNOWN until measured.

The supplied audit record reports that an actual WSL run of the previous exercise produced the $209.36 baseline and passed its four original negative cases. It also reports independent probes showing two defects: NaN or Infinity in input_rate_per_1000 could produce a NaN or Infinity subtotal, and qualified_capacity_gate(4.5, 700, 2400, 1) could return True despite fractional GPU units. Those are reports about the previous code, not claims that the replacement code below was executed during this drafting step.

The replacement validates every mapping and required field before arithmetic. Numeric values must be real finite numbers, must not be Boolean values, and must be nonnegative where appropriate. Days, request counts, token counts, installed GPU counts, and reserve GPU counts must be whole numbers. Pricing denominators must be finite, positive, and no greater than the exercise's explicit safety limit of 1,000,000,000. Reserve units cannot exceed installed units. Invalid input raises a controlled ValueError instead of producing a subtotal or capacity decision.

The offline exercise preserves the four original negative behaviors and adds an independent 12-case validation matrix. The matrix covers a non-mapping case, missing numeric and gate fields, NaN, positive Infinity, negative Infinity, a fractional request count, a Boolean used as a number, a zero denominator, fractional installed units, fractional reserve units, and reserve greater than installed units. Each case requires an exact ValueError message. These are expected tests in the replacement code. No execution of the replacement is claimed here.

Independent changed-input task: Change Case A to 1,000 requests per day, 1,500 input tokens and 500 output tokens per request, $0.001 per 1,000 input tokens, $0.003 per 1,000 output tokens, $220 monthly support, and $35 egress. Keep the $450 cloud catalog or serverless, $2,990 managed-compute, and $3,860 self-hosting assumptions unchanged. The workload remains connected, the fictional data-review gate passes, the availability target remains 99.5 percent, and the team still has only 0.15 operations staff-month, defined here as 24 available hours. Calculate monthly input and output tokens and the managed-API conditional subtotal. Compare the options, identify whether staffing or cost drives the decision, and name evidence that prevents unconditional approval.

Answer key: Monthly input tokens are 1,000 x 30 x 1,500 = 45,000,000. Monthly output tokens are 1,000 x 30 x 500 = 15,000,000. The managed-API conditional subtotal is (45,000 x $0.001) + (15,000 x $0.003) + $220 + $35 = $45 + $45 + $220 + $35 = $345.00 per month. License cost remains UNKNOWN, so complete TCO is UNKNOWN. The unchanged comparison subtotals are $450 for cloud catalog or serverless, $2,990 for managed compute, and $3,860 for self-hosting. Managed API remains the lowest fictional subtotal. Limited staffing independently blocks the two operationally heavier options because their required owner, backup, and on-call coverage is not demonstrated. Cost and staffing therefore both support the provisional managed-API recommendation after hard gates, but neither constitutes approval. Missing evidence can include exact license terms, artifact digest, measured quota and latency, retention terms, quality and safety results, or a documented fallback test.

Independent Case B key: Four installed units at 700 tokens per second provide 2,800 tokens per second before reserve. Reserving one failed unit leaves 3 x 700 = 2,100 tokens per second. Because 2,100 is less than the 2,400-token-per-second demand, the N-1 gate returns False. The result is a planning-gate failure, not proof of real capacity. Actual qualified capacity remains UNKNOWN until measured.

Expected output from an unmodified successful run of the replacement is: monthly_input_tokens=7200000; monthly_output_tokens=1800000; managed_api_conditional_subtotal=$209.36; license_cost=UNKNOWN; decision=managed_api_conditional_not_approval; case_b_one_gpu_reserve_passes=False; legacy_negative_cases_passed=4/4; validation_matrix_cases_passed=12/12; changed_monthly_input_tokens=45000000; changed_monthly_output_tokens=15000000; changed_managed_api_conditional_subtotal=$345.00; expected_output=matched. The final JSON line contains the same supported fields in machine-readable form.

Feedback for the task: If monthly token counts are multiplied by 30 twice, remove the extra factor. If all tokens are charged at the input rate, restore separate input and output rates. If $209.36 or $345.00 is labeled TCO, change it to conditional subtotal because license cost is UNKNOWN. If four units are accepted solely because 2,800 exceeds 2,400, apply the one-unit reserve and compare 2,100 with 2,400. If a fictional Boolean gate is treated as procurement evidence or a conditional recommendation is called approval, the decision has exceeded its evidence.

code.label: Offline standard-library exercise with finite-number, whole-count, shape, gate, and reserve validation
code.code:
import json
import math
from collections.abc import Mapping

HOURS_PER_STAFF_MONTH = 160
MAX_PRICING_DENOMINATOR = 1_000_000_000

# All rates, costs, capacities, and Boolean gates are fictional teaching fixtures.
# True gate values make the arithmetic exercise runnable. They are not real proof.
fixtures = {
    "requests_per_day": 200,
    "days": 30,
    "input_tokens_per_request": 1200,
    "output_tokens_per_request": 300,
    "input_rate_per_1000": 0.0008,
    "output_rate_per_1000": 0.0020,
    "support": 180.0,
    "egress": 20.0,
    "license_verified": True,
    "data_boundary_passed": True,
    "slo_evidence_passed": True,
    "owner_named": True,
    "backup_named": True,
    "on_call_defined": True
}

COUNT_FIELDS = (
    "requests_per_day",
    "days",
    "input_tokens_per_request",
    "output_tokens_per_request"
)
MONEY_FIELDS = (
    "input_rate_per_1000",
    "output_rate_per_1000",
    "support",
    "egress"
)
GATE_FIELDS = (
    "license_verified",
    "data_boundary_passed",
    "slo_evidence_passed",
    "owner_named",
    "backup_named",
    "on_call_defined"
)

def require_mapping(value, label):
    if not isinstance(value, Mapping):
        raise ValueError(label + " must be a mapping")
    return value

def require_present(mapping, key):
    if key not in mapping:
        raise ValueError("missing field: " + key)
    return mapping[key]

def require_finite_number(value, key, nonnegative=True):
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
        raise ValueError(key + " must be a number, not bool")
    if not math.isfinite(value):
        raise ValueError(key + " must be finite")
    if nonnegative and value < 0:
        raise ValueError(key + " must be nonnegative")
    return value

def require_whole_count(value, key):
    value = require_finite_number(value, key)
    if not float(value).is_integer():
        raise ValueError(key + " must be a whole number")
    return int(value)

def require_pricing_denominator(value):
    value = require_finite_number(value, "pricing_denominator", nonnegative=False)
    if value <= 0 or value > MAX_PRICING_DENOMINATOR:
        raise ValueError("pricing_denominator must be positive and reasonable")
    return value

def validate_pricing_case(case, pricing_denominator):
    case = require_mapping(case, "case")
    denominator = require_pricing_denominator(pricing_denominator)
    counts = {}
    for key in COUNT_FIELDS:
        counts[key] = require_whole_count(require_present(case, key), key)
    money = {}
    for key in MONEY_FIELDS:
        money[key] = require_finite_number(require_present(case, key), key)
    gates = {}
    for key in GATE_FIELDS:
        value = require_present(case, key)
        if not isinstance(value, bool):
            raise ValueError(key + " must be bool")
        gates[key] = value
    if not gates["license_verified"]:
        raise ValueError("license evidence missing")
    if not gates["data_boundary_passed"]:
        raise ValueError("data boundary failed")
    if not gates["slo_evidence_passed"]:
        raise ValueError("SLO evidence missing")
    if not (gates["owner_named"] and gates["backup_named"] and gates["on_call_defined"]):
        raise ValueError("staffing coverage missing")
    return counts, money, denominator

def managed_api_conditional_subtotal(case, pricing_denominator=1000):
    counts, money, denominator = validate_pricing_case(case, pricing_denominator)
    input_tokens = (
        counts["requests_per_day"]
        * counts["days"]
        * counts["input_tokens_per_request"]
    )
    output_tokens = (
        counts["requests_per_day"]
        * counts["days"]
        * counts["output_tokens_per_request"]
    )
    subtotal = (
        input_tokens / denominator * money["input_rate_per_1000"]
        + output_tokens / denominator * money["output_rate_per_1000"]
        + money["support"]
        + money["egress"]
    )
    if not math.isfinite(subtotal):
        raise ValueError("conditional subtotal must be finite")
    return input_tokens, output_tokens, round(subtotal, 2)

def qualified_capacity_gate(units, qualified_tps, demand_tps, reserve_units=0):
    units = require_whole_count(units, "units")
    reserve_units = require_whole_count(reserve_units, "reserve_units")
    qualified_tps = require_finite_number(qualified_tps, "qualified_tps")
    demand_tps = require_finite_number(demand_tps, "demand_tps")
    if qualified_tps <= 0:
        raise ValueError("qualified_tps must be positive")
    if reserve_units > units:
        raise ValueError("reserve exceeds installed units")
    usable_units = units - reserve_units
    return usable_units * qualified_tps >= demand_tps

def changed_case():
    case = dict(fixtures)
    case.update({
        "requests_per_day": 1000,
        "input_tokens_per_request": 1500,
        "output_tokens_per_request": 500,
        "input_rate_per_1000": 0.001,
        "output_rate_per_1000": 0.003,
        "support": 220.0,
        "egress": 35.0
    })
    return case

def without(mapping, key):
    result = dict(mapping)
    del result[key]
    return result

def expect_value_error(label, thunk, expected_message):
    try:
        thunk()
    except ValueError as exc:
        if str(exc) != expected_message:
            raise AssertionError(
                label + " expected " + repr(expected_message)
                + " but received " + repr(str(exc))
            )
        return
    raise AssertionError(label + " did not raise ValueError")

input_tokens, output_tokens, api_subtotal = managed_api_conditional_subtotal(fixtures)
case_b_one_gpu_reserve_passes = qualified_capacity_gate(
    4, 700, 2400, reserve_units=1
)
changed_input, changed_output, changed_subtotal = (
    managed_api_conditional_subtotal(changed_case())
)

legacy_negative_matrix = [
    (
        "negative token count",
        lambda: managed_api_conditional_subtotal(
            dict(fixtures, input_tokens_per_request=-1)
        ),
        "input_tokens_per_request must be nonnegative"
    ),
    (
        "missing license evidence",
        lambda: managed_api_conditional_subtotal(
            dict(fixtures, license_verified=False)
        ),
        "license evidence missing"
    ),
    (
        "missing SLO evidence",
        lambda: managed_api_conditional_subtotal(
            dict(fixtures, slo_evidence_passed=False)
        ),
        "SLO evidence missing"
    ),
    (
        "malformed backup gate",
        lambda: managed_api_conditional_subtotal(
            dict(fixtures, backup_named="unknown")
        ),
        "backup_named must be bool"
    )
]

validation_matrix = [
    (
        "non-mapping case",
        lambda: managed_api_conditional_subtotal([]),
        "case must be a mapping"
    ),
    (
        "missing numeric field",
        lambda: managed_api_conditional_subtotal(without(fixtures, "egress")),
        "missing field: egress"
    ),
    (
        "missing gate field",
        lambda: managed_api_conditional_subtotal(without(fixtures, "owner_named")),
        "missing field: owner_named"
    ),
    (
        "NaN rate",
        lambda: managed_api_conditional_subtotal(
            dict(fixtures, input_rate_per_1000=float("nan"))
        ),
        "input_rate_per_1000 must be finite"
    ),
    (
        "positive Infinity rate",
        lambda: managed_api_conditional_subtotal(
            dict(fixtures, input_rate_per_1000=float("inf"))
        ),
        "input_rate_per_1000 must be finite"
    ),
    (
        "negative Infinity rate",
        lambda: managed_api_conditional_subtotal(
            dict(fixtures, input_rate_per_1000=float("-inf"))
        ),
        "input_rate_per_1000 must be finite"
    ),
    (
        "fractional request count",
        lambda: managed_api_conditional_subtotal(
            dict(fixtures, requests_per_day=4.5)
        ),
        "requests_per_day must be a whole number"
    ),
    (
        "Boolean numeric field",
        lambda: managed_api_conditional_subtotal(
            dict(fixtures, days=True)
        ),
        "days must be a number, not bool"
    ),
    (
        "zero pricing denominator",
        lambda: managed_api_conditional_subtotal(
            fixtures, pricing_denominator=0
        ),
        "pricing_denominator must be positive and reasonable"
    ),
    (
        "fractional installed units",
        lambda: qualified_capacity_gate(4.5, 700, 2400, 1),
        "units must be a whole number"
    ),
    (
        "fractional reserve units",
        lambda: qualified_capacity_gate(4, 700, 2400, 1.5),
        "reserve_units must be a whole number"
    ),
    (
        "reserve exceeds installed units",
        lambda: qualified_capacity_gate(4, 700, 2400, 5),
        "reserve exceeds installed units"
    )
]

for label, thunk, message in legacy_negative_matrix:
    expect_value_error(label, thunk, message)
for label, thunk, message in validation_matrix:
    expect_value_error(label, thunk, message)

expected = {
    "case_b_one_gpu_reserve_passes": False,
    "changed_managed_api_conditional_subtotal": 345.0,
    "changed_monthly_input_tokens": 45000000,
    "changed_monthly_output_tokens": 15000000,
    "decision": "managed_api_conditional_not_approval",
    "legacy_negative_cases_passed": 4,
    "license_cost": "UNKNOWN",
    "managed_api_conditional_subtotal": 209.36,
    "monthly_input_tokens": 7200000,
    "monthly_output_tokens": 1800000,
    "validation_matrix_cases_passed": 12
}
actual = {
    "case_b_one_gpu_reserve_passes": case_b_one_gpu_reserve_passes,
    "changed_managed_api_conditional_subtotal": changed_subtotal,
    "changed_monthly_input_tokens": changed_input,
    "changed_monthly_output_tokens": changed_output,
    "decision": "managed_api_conditional_not_approval",
    "legacy_negative_cases_passed": len(legacy_negative_matrix),
    "license_cost": "UNKNOWN",
    "managed_api_conditional_subtotal": api_subtotal,
    "monthly_input_tokens": input_tokens,
    "monthly_output_tokens": output_tokens,
    "validation_matrix_cases_passed": len(validation_matrix)
}
assert actual == expected

print("monthly_input_tokens=" + str(input_tokens))
print("monthly_output_tokens=" + str(output_tokens))
print("managed_api_conditional_subtotal=$" + format(api_subtotal, ".2f"))
print("license_cost=UNKNOWN")
print("decision=managed_api_conditional_not_approval")
print("case_b_one_gpu_reserve_passes=" + str(case_b_one_gpu_reserve_passes))
print("legacy_negative_cases_passed=4/4")
print("validation_matrix_cases_passed=12/12")
print("changed_monthly_input_tokens=" + str(changed_input))
print("changed_monthly_output_tokens=" + str(changed_output))
print(
    "changed_managed_api_conditional_subtotal=$"
    + format(changed_subtotal, ".2f")
)
print("expected_output=matched")
print(json.dumps(expected, sort_keys=True))
